subject: Pilot readiness: synthesized discovery notes + prompt-batch request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Carla Gomez <carla.gomez@novapay.com>, Samir Khalid <samir.khalid@novapay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot readiness: synthesized discovery notes + prompt-batch request

Hi Carla / Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick synthesized recap and concrete asks so we can get the pilot baseline running next week.

Recap (short):
- Target: U.S. merchant dispute triage assistant (classification + suggested responses).
- Success criteria: 85% precision on merchant-match and <1.0s median inference latency for 2k qps simulated via Dedicated pool.
- Data constraints: no PII in shared prompts; customer can provide redacted text or IT can supply original with redaction guidance.

Initial model recommendations for evaluation (starting point):
1) llama-2-13b-chat (unquantized) — strong instruction-following baseline for safety checks
2) mistral-7b-instruct (8-bit quant) — cost-efficient candidate for throughput tests
3) falcon-40b-instruct (16-bit or 8-bit with perf profile) — for quality headroom if latency budget permits

Why these: mixes a high-quality mid/large model for accuracy checks and smaller cost-focused variants to explore unit-economics. We’ll run generation/QA and embedding+rerank passes to simulate your two-stage flow.

Concrete asks from NovaPay (what we need to run an initial eval):
- 150–300 representative customer prompts and 40–60 edge-case/rare prompts (examples: ambiguous merchant names, mixed language, heavy abbreviations). Please attach as CSV with columns: id, prompt_text, expected_label (if available), redaction_flag.
- A short list of three sample dialogs that should definitely not surface (safety/PII examples) so we can tune filters.
- Any internal redaction rules or a sample redaction map (e.g., replace card numbers with <CARD>, names with <NAME>).

Files & links: I’m attaching a template CSV (novapay_sample_prompts_v1.csv) and the call notes PDF. We’ve also provisioned an eval folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNOVAPAY-benchmarks and created eval record NDX-2027-087 in the Redwood evals dashboard.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Carla/Samir: share the prompt CSV + edge-case set by Tue 8/24. (ask: include redaction_flag column)
- Ben (cc’d): will spin up the three model evals and share an initial benchmark report by Thu 8/26.
- Irene (cc’d): will validate security/compliance constraints for Private/Dedicated deployment and flag anything that needs review by Mon 8/23.

If anything here isn’t correct or you want different models prioritized let me know — otherwise we’ll proceed on the dates above.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: novapay_sample_prompts_v1.csv (template), discovery-notes-20270818.pdf
From: Carla Gomez <carla.gomez@novapay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Khalid <samir.khalid@novapay.com>
Date: 2027-08-18T20:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: synthesized discovery notes + prompt-batch request

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. We’ve started pulling prompts and attached an initial batch (novapay_sample_prompts_v1.csv). A few notes:
- The file contains ~160 prompts (mixed real examples with tokenized redactions). We flagged ~18 edge cases in the edgecase column.
- Redaction approach: we replaced PANs and SSNs with <CARD> and <SSN>. For names we used <NAME>. If you need original text, we can set up an SFTP transfer with our security team (Samir looped).
- A couple of immediate concerns: our ops team is nervous about hallucinations when the model infers merchant intent — can you include example rejection triggers and a confidence threshold test in the eval?

Attachments: novapay_sample_prompts_v1.csv

Carla Gomez
Product Lead, Fraud Ops
NovaPay
carla.gomez@novapay.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Carla Gomez <carla.gomez@novapay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-19T07:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: synthesized discovery notes + prompt-batch request

Carla — perfect, thanks for the file and the redaction notes. Quick replies to your items and the plan update: 

1) We’ll include a hallucination/regression check: Ben will create a confidence threshold sweep and run the classification head with calibration to produce a precision/recall vs. threshold curve (we’ll recommend a default threshold and also a conservative fallback to return "manual review" when confidence < X).

2) Edge-case handling: we’ll mark the flagged edgecases as a separate holdout and include per-case failure analysis.

3) Transfer of originals: Samir, if you can provision SFTP for one encrypted batch (labelled "originals_for_redaction") we’ll take it under an NDA addendum and run our internal redaction validation tools. If that’s slower, we can proceed with your redacted CSV for the first pass.

Timing update: Ben expects first benchmark artifacts (accuracy table + latency histogram + regression flags) by EOD Thu 8/26. Irene will confirm the compliance checklist by Mon 8/23 and flag any Private deployment gating items.

Action items (updated):
- Carla/Samir: confirm whether you’ll provide originals via SFTP or proceed with redacted CSV only (reply by 8/20).
- Ben: run initial evals on the three model candidates and include confidence threshold sweep (deliverable 8/26).
- Irene: security checklist for Dedicated/Private and notes on KMS/HSM for data-at-rest (deliverable 8/23).

I’ll schedule a short sync (15m) for Wed 8/24 to review initial results if that works for you.

Thanks — Jonas
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Carla Gomez <carla.gomez@novapay.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-19T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot readiness: synthesized discovery notes + prompt-batch request

Ack — I’ve started the eval jobs on the three models Jonas listed. Quick notes:
- Running small-batch tokenized runs to validate prompt parsing first, then scale to 1k-simulated queries for latency profiling.
- Will add a confidence sweep and a simple heuristic-based rejection baseline to compare against model-based scores.
- Deliverables: initial accuracy matrix, per-case failure list, latency histograms, and a short doc with recommended thresholds. Will upload to the drive link and post the eval id to the Redwood dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/NDX-2027-087

If you run into anything in the CSV (formatting oddities), ping me directly and I’ll patch the ingestion.

—Ben
